April 2026 slide: 0.5% fill from 2028 (read from the timeline figure, not from text), '0.5% data' after it, 'Fill 1.5% Te' around 2030-2032 and '1.5% data' last; "0.5%: best sensitivity to 130Te 0vbb (2x10^26 yr in 3 yrs). Submitted proposal for 1.5% loading". A schedule, not an event.

intervals.label: acrylic vessel leak repair
intervals.note: Added 2026-10-25. LIP Advisory Committee slide (27-28 April 2026, J. Maneira): "Acrylic Vessel Repairs: leak in AV, height identified, lowering water now to repair, autumn restart". SNOLAB report of 26 May 2026 has a slide 'SNO+ Cavity Access for Repairs' (rope-access team, boat in the cavity, "No damage to the neck. AV was not stuck", "Installing lights"; photo of the cavity with the water level lowered), so the repair was under way in spring 2026. No source gives the day the scintillator data-taking stopped (the April 2026 reactor analysis, arXiv:2604.05746, uses data "between May 2022 and July 2025", which is an analysis cut, not an end of running), so the start is 'by April 2026' at month precision, approximate. The restart is a plan: 'autumn restart' (autumn 2026 = September-November, middle month 2026-10); the slide does not say what restarts (scintillator data-taking or water fill) and no source dated after 26 May 2026 reports it, so the shutdown is kept at 2026-10-25 and must be re-checked.
intervals.quote: leak in AV, height identified, lowering water now to repair, autumn restart

summary.plain: SNO+ reuses the same underground cavern and acrylic ball that SNO used, now filled with liquid scintillator, to search for a hypothetical nuclear decay and to study solar and reactor neutrinos.
summary.technical: Multipurpose experiment at SNOLAB reusing SNO's acrylic vessel and cavern: water-fill commissioning 2017-2019, then 780 t liquid-scintillator fill from 2022, with a planned future tellurium-loading phase for a neutrinoless double-beta-decay search; also measures 8B solar neutrinos and long-baseline reactor antineutrino oscillations.

unique_capabilities.value: Reuses the original SNO acrylic vessel and cavern, refilled first with water, then liquid scintillator, and eventually tellurium-loaded scintillator, for a multi-phase, multi-purpose physics program
